Philosophy
GREENBOX's philosophy focuses on creating atmospheric and high-quality open spaces. The firm sees it as its task and responsibility to design open spaces that are not only functional, but also aesthetically pleasing and sustainable. This approach is particularly reflected in the planning and implementation of squares, promenades, parks, and open spaces, which are always integrated into an urban context. GREENBOX places great emphasis on a close connection between architecture and landscape in order to develop holistic and customized solutions for each location. Through intensive dialogue with the relevant stakeholders and a detailed examination of the location where a project is being implemented, open spaces are created that possess a strong identity and optimally meet the needs of the local people.

Strategic Orientation
GREENBOX's vision for the future and strategic direction are strongly aligned with the challenges of a changing society, particularly with regard to the effects of climate change and the increasing demands for sustainable, livable open spaces. The company strives to create competitive advantages through the use of modern, digital technologies and innovative working approaches. A central goal is to further expand internal structures and optimize processes in order to work even more efficiently.GREENBOX is aware of its responsibility to develop long-term, sustainable solutions that meet the needs of people and nature. With openness, curiosity, and creativity, the firm implements projects that offer individual solutions. The integration of digital technologies into the planning process plays a central role in creating holistic solutions. In addition to technical and creative development, GREENBOX places particular emphasis on developing its team. The goal is to be perceived as one of the most attractive employers in the industry by offering employees optimal conditions for their personal and professional development. The focus is on a collegial, appreciative working environment that fosters team spirit.

Core Competencies
GREENBOX's services encompass the entire spectrum of landscape architecture, from urban open space planning and renaturation to greening concepts and stormwater management. The firm supports construction projects from the initial assessment through design and execution planning to construction management. Complex tasks such as cost control and quality management are also handled, which are particularly crucial for large-scale projects with construction costs of more than €10 million for open spaces. Another key component of GREENBOX's work is participation in competitions. The firm views this as an essential building block of a vibrant building culture, in which new ideas and creative approaches are regularly tested and developed further. GREENBOX works in an interdisciplinary manner, collaborating with architects, urban planners, landscape and gardening companies, environmental planners, project developers, and many more, to examine projects from different perspectives and thus develop sustainable and viable concepts.
GREENBOX's main clients include municipalities and public clients, as well as large companies and private investors. The firm operates primarily in Germany, but has also participated in international projects in the past. Through its many years of experience in dealing with large-scale construction projects, GREENBOX has developed a deep understanding of the needs and requirements of cities and municipalities, which is reflected in the high quality of its implemented projects.

description: SensiPhi is an advanced optical fibre sensing company specialising in the design and development of High-Resolution Distributed Acoustic Sensing (HR-DAS) technology. Our core innovation transforms standard optical fibres into dense, large-scale arrays of virtual sensors capable of detecting and localising vibrations and strain with exceptional detail. Using HR-DAS, a single fibre optic cable becomes a continuous sensor capable of capturing vibration data at thousands of points along its length, with each point sampled at rates up to 1 million samples per second (1 MSPS). This level of resolution enables detection of high-frequency acoustic signals, including ultrasonic vibrations, making it a powerful tool for non-destructive testing (NDT) and structural health monitoring (SHM). Because of the fibre’s small size and passive nature, it can be seamlessly embedded into carbon composite structures during manufacturing, enabling real-time, in-situ monitoring without adding significant weight or complexity. This makes the technology especially suitable for aerospace, space structures, and advanced materials research, where performance, reliability, and early fault detection are critical. SensiPhi’s HR-DAS platform supports a wide range of applications, including: Structural integrity monitoring of spacecraft and aircraft, Ultrasonic NDT for defect detection in composite materials, Vibration analysis for launch systems and ground support structures, and Environmental sensing in harsh or remote conditions. By enabling high-resolution, distributed sensing with minimal infrastructure, SensiPhi is redefining the way structures are monitored and understood, paving the way for safer, smarter, and more resilient aerospace systems.

entityDescription: Sapienza boasts a long tradition as a protagonist of international aerospace activities, which began in the 1960s when, thanks to the initiative of a group of professors led by Prof. Luigi Broglio, Italy became the third country in the world, after the United States and Russia, capable of launching a scientific satellite into orbit. Over 100 tenured professors work in this sector at Sapienza, carrying out research in all fields of interest in aerospace, often with excellent results, recognized internationally. The creation of the Sapienza Aerospace Research Center (CRAS), established in June 2008, was therefore essentially motivated by the aim of creating appropriate synergies and providing strong and unitary visibility to the sector. This created an interdepartmental structure for the coordination of research activities that professors carry out mainly in their own departments. Participation in the Center allows for coordinated and synergic operations, as well as providing visibility that goes beyond the boundaries of the individual department, but benefits from the highest representation provided by Sapienza. CRAS boasts important relationships with industrial entities, both Italian and international, and collaborations with public bodies and ministries. In the field of relationships with industrial entities, in addition to the collaborations activated at a national level, the Framework Agreement signed with EADS-Astrium is significant, which will provide our researchers with the opportunity to be included in important European projects.

entityDescription:
The Institute of Plant Protection – National Research Institute (IPP – NRI) is a public research unit supervised by the Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development, established on January 24, 1951. The main office of IPP – NRI is located in Poznań and the Branch Office is in Sośnicowice. The Institute also runs three Regional Experiment Stations: in Białystok, Toruń and Rzeszów, as well as a Field Experiment Station and an Agricultural Experiment Station in Winna Góra (Wielkopolska).
The Institute of Plant Protection provides research, implementation, promotion, and other services within the area of plant protection in Poland. The IPP – NRI performs its tasks as part of its statutory activity, financed by the Ministry of Science and Higher Education; the Multiannual Programme, financed by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, and various domestic and foreign projects (grants).
The Institute conducts studies pertaining to biology, harmfulness and methods of pest control, scientific basis of integrated plant protection, plant protection in organic farming, systems supporting decisions on the need to perform treatments, residues and quality of plant protection products, as well as Pest Risk Assessments (PRA). The IPP – NRI units are prepared to conduct research required in the registration process of plant protection products, fertilizers and biostimulators, crop plants, qualitative analysis of crops and risk assessment of pest resistance to plant protection products.
There are a number of well-equipped research units, unique for Poland, operating within the Institute:the Plant Diseases Clinic and Bank of Pathogens– providing services in the field of identification of viral, bacterial and fungal diseases of plants, andthe Research Centre of Quarantine, Invasive and Genetically Modified Organisms – a modern facility that meets the highest standards of phytosanitary safety (SL3). The following are the certified IPP – NRI units, authorized to conduct research on the effectiveness of all types of plant protection products: the Research Centre for Registration of Agrochemicalsin Poznań and the Pesticide Efficacy Testing Departmentin Sośnicowice, where a modern laboratory testing the quality, originality and residues of plant protection products is also operating. Within the Regional Experimental Station in Białystok, operates the Food and Feed Safety Laboratory, which conducts studies mainly on the use of plant protection products in crops for the risk of contamination of crops and food products with residues. The Institute also operates the Expert Centre of the Evaluation of Agrochemical Reports.
The Institute closely cooperates with government institutions, domestic and foreign research and development units, as well as with agricultural advisory centres and agricultural producers.
The Institute is authorised to confer doctoral and postdoctoral degrees in agricultural sciences in the field of agricultural sciences, namely agriculture and horticulture, and to conduct the procedure to confer the title of professor of agricultural sciences. IPP – NRI organises doctoral and postgraduate programmes, scientific sessions, conferences, seminars, workshops and trainings.
The IOR Hotel & Congress Centre– with 14 conference rooms fitted with audio-visual equipment (e.g. for simultaneous interpreting), 125 beds of various standards and attractive catering facilities, is perfect for both work and leisure.
